subject: Standardization and Bootstraped standard deviation in a mediation model

messages.author: f34d3726cfcbcd1d
messages.subject: Standardization and Bootstraped standard deviation in a mediation model
parts:
Hi,

I'm trying to estimate a mediation model with latent variables. Due to non-normality, I performed it using WLSMV.
I did not put integers in equations. As far as I understood I thus have to use the standardized coefficients displayed in the std.all column.
For the indirect effects, I would like to have the boostraped standard erros. I'm trying to perform it in two ways, either specifying se=bootstrap in the sem function, either using the boostraplavaan function. The first one is very slow on my computer (several days with 1000 draws) since I did not find how to ask for parralel. For the second solution, I'm not sure to understand what I obtain. I get min, mean, median... values which seems to be the bootstraped coefficients (and not the bootstraped standard errors). How can I directly get boostraped standard errors and the associated p-values ?

Below is my code.

Thank you very much for your help !

Best regards.
Hélène

### modèle M1

M1 <- '
#measurement model
X1 =~ i1+i2+i3
X2=~ i4+i5+i6
X3 =~ i7+i8+i9+i10
X4 =~ i11+i12+i13
X5 =~  i14+i15+i16+i17
X6=~i18+i19+i20+i21+i22
X7=~i23+i24+i25+i26+i27+i28+i29+i30
Y1 =~ j1+j2
Y2 =~ j3+j4

Z1 =~ X2+X3+X4
Z2 =~ X5+X6+X7

#regressions
Z2 ~ a0 * Z1+a1*X1
Y1 ~ b1 * Z2 + b2d * Z1+ b3d*X1+ b4*age + b5*age2+b6*urban+b7*size
Y2 ~  c2 * Z1 + c3*X1 + c4*age + c5*age2+c6*urban+c7*size

#covariances
Y1~~d0*Y2
X1~~ d1*Y1

#correlated residuals (reverse coded items)
i4 ~~ i5

i14~~ i15
i14~~ i16
i15~~i16

#indirect effects of Z1 on Y1
b2i:=a0*b1
b3i:=a1*b1

#total effect of Z1 on Y1
b2t:=a0*b1+b2d
b3t:=a1*b1+b3d
'
############
##Solution 1 :
fit_M1_boot <- sem(M1,data = epd_opi,se="bootstrap",test="scaled.shifted",
                   estimator="DWLS", verbose=F,bootstrap=1000L,
                   ordered=c("i1","i2","i3","i4","i5","i6","i7","i8","i9","i10","i11","i12","i13","i14","i15","i16","i17","i18","i19","i20","i21","i22","i23","i24","i25","i26","i27","i28","i29","i30","j1","j2","j3","j4")))
summary(fit_M1_boot, standardized = TRUE, fit.measures=TRUE,rsquare=T)


############
##Solution 2 :
fit_M1 <- sem(M1,data = epd_opi,estimator="WLSMV", verbose=F,                   ordered=c("i1","i2","i3","i4","i5","i6","i7","i8","i9","i10","i11","i12","i13","i14","i15","i16","i17","i18","i19","i20","i21","i22","i23","i24","i25","i26","i27","i28","i29","i30","j1","j2","j3","j4")))
summary(fit_M1, standardized = TRUE, fit.measures=TRUE,rsquare=T)

M1_boot<-bootstrapLavaan(fit_M1,R=1000L,type="ordinary", verbose=T,parallel="multicore",ncpus=36,FUN=function(x) standardizedSolution(x)$est.std))
summary(M1_boot)




fit_M1 <- sem(M1,data = epd_opi,estimator="WLSMV", verbose=T,
                   ordered=c("i1","i2","i3","i4","i5","i6","i7","i8","i9","i10","i11","i12","i13","i14","i15","i16","i17","i18","i19","i20","i21","i22","i23","i24","i25","i26","i27","i28","i29","i30","j1","j2","j3","j4")))

print(M1_boot<-bootstrapLavaan(fit_M1,R=10L,type="ordinary", verbose=T,parallel="multicore",ncpus=36,FUN=function(x) standardizedSolution(x)$est.std))

messages.author: 82889e926eb5165e
messages.subject: Re: Standardization and Bootstraped standard deviation in a mediation model
parts:
Helene

WLSMV may be slower for sampling methods like bootstrap. If time is an issue you have several options.
Your second solution gives you explicitly the parameter estimates for each bootstrap, each column will be a parameter and each row will be a different bootstrap, so you can ask the quantiles for each column to get the empirical confidence interval, like:
quantile(M1_boot[,1] , probs=c(.025,.975)) ## confidence interval for column 1, parameter 1

The other option would be to use the monteCarloMed function from semTools to aproximate the indirect effect

bye

messages.author: 82889e926eb5165e
messages.subject: Re: Standardization and Bootstraped standard deviation in a mediation model
parts:
Helene

With WLSMV with ordinal items you dont have intercepts, you have thresholds. I dont see why using this parametrisation it force you to use the std.all values. Specially interested in indurect effects, these effects are usually presented in their unstandardized value.
Unless I am missing something, the decision of using unstandardized or standardized values would be as in any other model. With the indirect effetcs I have only seen it as unstandardized values.

The reason to present the indirect effect as unstandarized would be beacuse they are calculated with the unstandardized parameters, a post standardization of it seems weird to me. A standardized indirect effect would have to be calculated by multiplying the standardized parameters. That would be my reasoning for the indirect effects, there may be another position

bye
